title: Hosted API runway and Model Catalog pruning: Q4 release map and OKR alignment
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: create an actionable, time-boxed Q4 roadmap that aligns Hosted API product runway (new API ergonomics, rate-limiting primitives, and streaming stability improvements) with a phased Model Catalog pruning and coherence plan. The goal is to reduce customer confusion about model families, lower operational costs by retiring redundant variants, and ensure rollout plans map to OKRs for reliability and unit economics.

Scope:
- Finalize model taxonomy and stable set for Hosted API (recommended default, low-latency variants, high-quality variants).
- Define deprecation windows and compatibility shims for clients.
- Schedule API surface changes (new routing policy knobs, default batching limits) with migration timelines.
- Coordinate canary and rollback playbooks with Eng and SRE for each catalog change.
- Tie milestones to OKRs: reliability (p99 latency), cost-per-1k-tokens, and catalog coverage metrics.

Out-of-scope: deep research on model quantization; larger Dedicated capacity billing model changes (to be handled in a follow-up initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Product decision finalized: canonical model set for Hosted API (list + rationale) published to Confluence

API surface change RFC approved by Architecture and Security
Canary/rollback playbooks validated in staging and rehearsed with SRE
OKR mapping: three measurable metrics with baseline and target values committed

key_decisions: Adopt three-tier model taxonomy (default, latencysensitive, high-quality) rather than per-architecture variants to simplify choices
Require 60-day minimum user notice for any deprecation impacting Hosted API defaults
Introduce a lightweight compatibility shim in SDKs to map retired model aliases to recommended defaults for 90 days
tradeoffs: Pruning aggressively reduces unit costs but increases short-term migration burden for some customers — mitigated via compatibility shim and extended notices
Keeping many model variants increases discoverability but raises operational and SLO complexity; chosen middle path reduces variants by ~30% in the canonical set
Delaying API surface cleanup reduces immediate engineering risk but slows alignment to OKR targets for latency/cost
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected customer regressions after deprecation. Mitigation: a staged canary rollout with signal thresholds and instant rollback policy.
Risk: Documentation and SDK updates lag behind platform changes. Mitigation: freeze for docs + SDK release window synchronized with platform deployments.
Risk: Metrics baseline noise (difficulty proving cost improvements). Mitigation: define controlled traffic slices and instrument token-level cost telemetry before changes
